summary: Right-footed soccer instep kick at ball contact: laces strike the ball centre, toes pointed and ankle locked, support knee bent, body over the ball.

cameras.name: side_low
cameras.text: Ground-level side view, laces meeting the ball, ball slightly deformed at impact.

cameras.name: goal_view
cameras.text: Goalkeeper's point of view, compressed telephoto perspective, sharp focus on the ball.

cameras.name: wide_cinema
cameras.text: Wide low frame, stadium lights and crowd blurred behind.

rules.why: kicking thigh swinging forward, knee over or just behind the ball (hip reported near neutral, -7 to 15 deg, against a tilted pelvis frame)
kicking knee still bent and extending at impact (about 43-67 deg)
ankle plantar-flexed and locked, toes pointed down
support knee about 42 deg flexion at contact
body over the ball, not leaning far back

text.action: a soccer player striking a right-footed instep shot, the laces hitting the centre of the ball
text.core: Left support foot planted flat beside the ball, left knee bent about 40 degrees; right kicking leg swinging through with the knee still slightly bent, ankle locked and toes pointed down, the top of the foot (laces) meeting the back centre of the ball; hips turned square to the goal; trunk over the ball; left arm out wide, right arm swinging across.
text.gaze: Head down over the ball, eyes on the contact point.
cues: toe pointed down and ankle locked
strike through the centre of the ball with the laces
hips square to the target at contact
knee over the ball keeps the shot low
kinetic: ball compressing against the laces, first frame of flight
grass spray and a small divot flying off the turf
motion blur on the kicking shin, support leg sharp

sources.cite: Kellis & Katis 2007, JSSM 6:154: at impact the hip is flexed, the knee extending, the ankle plantar-flexed
Systematic review of instep-kick kinematics in elite adult players (hip -7 to 15 deg, knee 67 +/- 19 deg at impact)
Lees et al. 2010, J Sports Sci review: support knee 42 deg at contact
Kapidzic et al. 2014: swinging-leg knee 136.5 deg included angle (about 43.5 deg flexion)
Nunome et al. 2002/2006: instep ball speed about 28 m/s, contact under 10 ms
